headline_marked: ACC [[probes corruption allegations against Asif Mahmud]] and ministry officials
headline: ACC probes corruption allegations against Asif Mahmud and ministry officials
summary: The Anti-Corruption Commission has sought records from the Youth and Sports Ministry regarding appointments, promotions, and transfers during the former advisor's tenure.
details: The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has requested four types of documents from the Ministry of Youth and Sports to investigate allegations of irregularities and corruption involving former advisor Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan and other officials.
The ACC sent a letter to the ministry's secretary on Thursday, requesting that the required documents be submitted to the ACC headquarters by September 10.
Other officials under investigation include former secretary Moh. Mahbub-ul-Alam, Joint Secretary Dr. Sheikh Mohammad Zubaid Hossain, and Deputy Secretary Moh. Masum Ahmed.
A four-member team led by ACC Deputy Director Moh. Zahid Kalam was formed on Wednesday to investigate the claims.
Allegations suggest that 7.6 million BDT was taken to cancel the current duties of 38 Upazila Youth Development Officers and appoint them to new positions.

It is further alleged that 15 million BDT was collected from 150 Assistant Upazila Youth Development Officers for promotions, and another 20 million BDT was exchanged for postings in preferred locations.

The probe is examining whether a syndicate was formed with the support of the former advisor and high-ranking ministry officials to engage in trade regarding transfers and promotions, as well as corruption in procurement and tenders.
caption:
Millions of BDT allegedly exchanged for promotions and postings. The ACC is now probing former advisor Asif Mahmud.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has requested four types of documents from the Ministry of Youth and Sports to investigate allegations of irregularities and corruption involving former advisor Asif Mahmud Sajeeb Bhuiyan and other officials.

The ACC sent a letter to the ministry's secretary on Thursday, requesting that the required documents be submitted to the ACC headquarters by September 10.

Other officials under investigation include former secretary Moh. Mahbub-ul-Alam, Joint Secretary Dr. Sheikh Mohammad Zubaid Hossain, and Deputy Secretary Moh. Masum Ahmed.

A four-member team led by ACC Deputy Director Moh. Zahid Kalam was formed on Wednesday to investigate the claims.

Allegations suggest that 7.6 million BDT was taken to cancel the current duties of 38 Upazila Youth Development Officers and appoint them to new positions.

It is further alleged that 15 million BDT was collected from 150 Assistant Upazila Youth Development Officers for promotions, and another 20 million BDT was exchanged for postings in preferred locations.

The probe is examining whether a syndicate was formed with the support of the former advisor and high-ranking ministry officials to engage in trade regarding transfers and promotions, as well as corruption in procurement and tenders.

headline_marked: Mirza Abbas [[returns to parliament in wheelchair]] after medical treatment abroad
headline: Mirza Abbas returns to parliament in wheelchair after medical treatment abroad
summary: The BNP lawmaker and PM's Political Adviser gave an emotional maiden speech in the 13th Jatiya Sangsad after recovering from brain surgery.
details: BNP lawmaker and Prime Minister's Political Adviser Mirza Abbas returned to the parliament today, delivering an emotional maiden speech in the 13th Jatiya Sangsad.
Entering the chamber in a wheelchair at 3:50pm, Abbas was welcomed by Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad and greeted by fellow MPs with table-thumping.
In his speech, Abbas described the moment as 'deeply emotional and historic,' stating that he has returned to serve the people and Bangladesh after nearly two decades.
He expressed gratitude to the president, the prime minister, and the Prime Minister's Office for their support and for checking on him during his illness.
Abbas, a veteran politician and former housing minister, had fallen seriously ill on the eve of the first parliamentary session, collapsing during iftar on March 11.
He underwent brain surgery in Dhaka before being flown by air ambulance to Singapore and later transferred to Malaysia for physiotherapy and rehabilitation.
The lawmaker sought prayers from his colleagues for continued health and strength to serve his constituency and the 대해 nation with dedication.
caption:
After brain surgery and months of treatment abroad, Mirza Abbas returns to the Jatiya Sangsad in a wheelchair.

BNP lawmaker and Prime Minister's Political Adviser Mirza Abbas returned to the parliament today, delivering an emotional maiden speech in the 13th Jatiya Sangsad.

Entering the chamber in a wheelchair at 3:50pm, Abbas was welcomed by Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad and greeted by fellow MPs with table-thumping.

In his speech, Abbas described the moment as 'deeply emotional and historic,' stating that he has returned to serve the people and Bangladesh after nearly two decades.

He expressed gratitude to the president, the prime minister, and the Prime Minister's Office for their support and for checking on him during his illness.

Abbas, a veteran politician and former housing minister, had fallen seriously ill on the eve of the first parliamentary session, collapsing during iftar on March 11.

He underwent brain surgery in Dhaka before being flown by air ambulance to Singapore and later transferred to Malaysia for physiotherapy and rehabilitation.

The lawmaker sought prayers from his colleagues for continued health and strength to serve his constituency and the 대해 nation with dedication.
